name: L40S
notes: The official L40S datasheet PDF could not be directly downloaded (signed CDN URLs on nvdam.widen.net returned 404, live and archived) -- figures instead sourced from the equivalent official specs table embedded directly in the live nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/l40s/ page HTML, not a third-party mirror. Both dense and with-sparsity figures are independently given by NVIDIA for TF32/BF16/FP16/FP8/INT8 on this page (unlike L4, where only sparse was given and dense had to be derived). INT4 Tensor Core is listed on the page with figures identical to INT8 (733/1466 TOPS) -- reported as-is per NVIDIA's own table without assuming it's a copy-paste error, but not recorded as a separate schema field since this schema has no int4 field; flagging here for future reference. NVLink explicitly stated as unsupported ('NVIDIA NVLink Support: No'). Multi-Instance GPU explicitly stated as unsupported ('Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) Support: No') on the same page. sm_count not stated anywhere on the page. gpu_chip of AD102: NVIDIA's own 'Ada GPU Architecture' whitepaper directly confirms AD102 for the original L40 (Appendix C, Table 4: 'GPU Code Name: AD102'), but does NOT mention 'L40S' by that name -- L40S's own AD102 attribution rests on well-corroborated third-party consensus (TechPowerUp, videocardz.net, ServeTheHome, Thunder Compute all independently agree L40S uses AD102-896, a different bin/revision from L40's AD102-895) rather than a verbatim NVIDIA statement naming L40S specifically. process_node_nm of 4 (TSMC 4N) carries the same indirect-but-strong sourcing: NVIDIA's whitepaper confirms TSMC 4N for AD102 generally (in its RTX 4090 comparison table), and L40S shares that die per the third-party consensus above; one third-party outlier (TechPowerUp) numerically labels the node '5 nm' while still calling it '4N custom process' elsewhere -- consistent with the same TSMC-4N-naming-vs-numeric-node ambiguity noted for L4. release_date of 2023-08-08 is NVIDIA's SIGGRAPH 2023 announcement, distinct from L4's earlier GTC Spring 2023 date (2023-03-21) and from the original L40's still-earlier announcement (~October 2022) -- these are three separate announcement events, not one date reused across the Ada lineup.

_sources.gpu_chip: Indirect NVIDIA + third-party consensus: https://images.nvidia.com/aem-dam/Solutions/Data-Center/l4/nvidia-ada-gpu-architecture-whitepaper-V2.02.pdf confirms AD102 for sibling part L40 (not L40S by name); L40S's own AD102 attribution (AD102-896 bin) corroborated by techpowerup.com/gpu-specs/l40s.c4173, videocardz.net/nvidia-l40s, servethehome.com L40S launch coverage
_sources.process_node_nm: Indirect NVIDIA (whitepaper confirms TSMC 4N for AD102 generally) + third-party consensus naming L40S specifically: videocardz.net/nvidia-l40s ('4 nm (TSMC 4N)'), servethehome.com ('4nm NVIDIA Custom Process')
